title: Shambu — I am feeling breathlessness, please help me

remoteEncounter.guard: A remote consultation from home. He distrusts doctors he cannot meet in person and is guarded — building confidence is the challenge, not the physical exam.
beats: Acknowledging the remote setting and its limits.
Reassuring him that his reports will be read carefully despite the distance.
Closing with a clear follow-up plan.

expectation.management: Metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals, dietary changes, daily walking, and a home glucometer. Review in 1 month with a repeat HbA1c.

P.name: Shambu
P.publicProfile: Male, 72, retired schoolteacher, lives alone in Prayagraj, consulting from home. Uneasy about the distance of a remote consult. He complains of breathlessness on walking, tiredness, and drinking more water than usual.
P.secret: Has been drinking a lot of water and getting up 3-4 times a night to pass urine for months. A small cut on his foot has not healed. He distrusts doctors he cannot meet face to face and nearly ended the consult before it began.
topics: How have you been feeling lately?
Are you drinking more water than usual?
Do you get up at night to pass urine?
Can I look at your blood test report?

F.name: Priya
F.secret: She set up this remote consult and coaxed her grandfather into it. She has noticed he is thinner than last winter and that his mother had diabetes.
topics: Why did you set up this remote consult?
Have you noticed changes in your grandfather?
Is there any family history of illness?

R.name: Sister Aagya
R.secret: The file shows a raised random blood glucose reading from two years ago that was never followed up. Nothing else of note.
topics: Was anything abnormal two years ago?
Is there a history of high sugar?

syntheticReports.label: Fasting Blood Glucose Report
syntheticReports.caption: Fasting blood glucose report — handed over by the patient
syntheticReports.finding: Fasting plasma glucose 168 mg/dL and post-meal 232 mg/dL — elevated, consistent with diabetes.
syntheticReports.patientReaction: "The lab wallah gave me this paper last week, doctor. I didn't know what it meant."
syntheticReports.hint: I got a blood test done last week, doctor — the report is on my table, I can show it to you.

syntheticReports.label: HbA1c Report
syntheticReports.caption: Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) report — handed over by the patient
lines: Interpretation: confirms a high average blood sugar over 3 months
syntheticReports.finding: HbA1c 8.4% — confirms elevated average blood sugar over the past 3 months.
syntheticReports.patientReaction: "The same lab did this longer sugar test, doctor. They said my sugar is high these months."
syntheticReports.hint: The lab also did that longer-term sugar test, doctor — the paper's with the other reports.

clues.label: Increased thirst
clues.shortText: Drinking far more water than usual for weeks.
clues.longText: Shambu has been drinking a lot more water than usual for the past several weeks, even at night. His granddaughter first noticed the empty water jug.

clues.label: Nocturia
clues.shortText: Getting up 3-4 times a night to pass urine.
clues.longText: He wakes 3 to 4 times every night to pass urine, which has never happened before. It interrupts his sleep and he feels tired the next day.

clues.label: Fatigue
clues.shortText: Tired most of the day, especially after meals.
clues.longText: He has felt tired most of the day for weeks, especially a heaviness in the early afternoon. He used to walk to the market daily and now rests instead.

clues.label: Weight loss
clues.shortText: Lost about 4 kg over 3 months without trying.
clues.longText: He has lost roughly four kilograms over three months without changing his diet. His kurta fits loosely now.

clues.label: Blurry vision
clues.longText: His vision blurs off and on, more in the evenings. He had been blaming old age and his spectacles.

clues.label: Slow-healing cut
clues.shortText: A small cut on his foot has not healed in weeks.
clues.longText: A small cut on his left foot from weeks ago has not healed. He mentions it and describes it as dry and refusing to close. He had been ignoring it.

clues.label: Foot tingling
clues.shortText: Tingling in his feet at night.
clues.longText: He feels a tingling or pins-and-needles in both feet, worse at night, which he finds hard to describe.

clues.label: Granddaughter's concern
clues.shortText: Priya noticed he is thinner and drinking a lot.
clues.longText: Priya says he is noticeably thinner than last winter and has been drinking a lot of water. She persuaded him to try this remote consult.

clues.label: Family history of diabetes
clues.longText: Priya recalls that her grandmother (Shambu's mother) had 'sugar' and took medicines for years before she passed.

clues.label: Old raised glucose
clues.shortText: File: a raised random glucose two years ago, never followed up.
clues.longText: The file records a random blood glucose of 198 mg/dL from a health-camp screening two years ago, with no follow-up action taken.

clues.label: Fasting glucose: 168
clues.shortText: Blood glucose report shows an elevated fasting level.
clues.longText: The fasting glucose report shows 168 mg/dL fasting and 232 mg/dL random — both clearly elevated.

clues.label: HbA1c: 8.4%
clues.shortText: HbA1c confirms 3 months of high blood sugar.
clues.longText: The HbA1c is 8.4%, confirming that the blood sugar has been high for months, not just on one reading.

clues.label: DIAGNOSIS
clues.longText: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Shambu is started on metformin with meals, dietary changes and daily walking, and is asked to check his sugar at home. A follow-up consult is booked in one month.
